core.title: Give each existing canonical documentation area an entry-point index
core.given: An authored documentation area — a canonical directory of the documentation tree that holds authored documents, as listed in the profile (the tree root itself is one such area) — exists, or your plan creates it.
core.when: The area lacks its entry-point index document, before or after your change.
core.then: The area MUST contain its entry-point index document — the area's entry point and the node the rendered documentation navigates to.
prefer: Give the index full document identity like any authored document in the tree: its own title, stable document id, and status.
Nothing to introduce? Ask whether the area should exist yet, not what its index says; grow the tree only for a real requirement.
In the decision-record area, the index is also a DERIVED registry, governed by the sibling derived-registry rule.
avoid: Ceremonial index or canonical files in every subdirectory, or to fill an empty taxonomy; directories holding two related documents need no landing page.
Creating an empty area just to index it.
Requiring an index in generated output trees.
unless: Generated output trees are never required to carry an index.
An absent area is not reported; only an existing area missing its index is.
core.why: Without an index, the rendered documentation cannot navigate into the area and a reader cannot enter it; scoping to the canonical areas deliberately avoids ceremonial files.
evidence: The stack's documentation-tree check reports no finding: every existing canonical area has its entry-point index.
A reviewer checks that each canonical area existing after the change — including the documentation tree's root area and untouched pre-existing areas — has its index.
verification: The check scans the documentation tree and covers exactly the canonical areas listed in the profile; it does not require an index in any other subdirectory.
Report only when an area directory exists and lacks its index; absent areas are not violations. Directory existence alone is sufficient, independent of file kinds or change type.

Generated output trees under the documentation tree are excluded entirely; no index is required there. This check owns its exact generated-output classification itself — it is not inferred from any stack-wide exclusion list — and the concrete generated-output tree is realization-specific.
Severity 3; disposition strict: the checker fails on every finding, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.
The violation predicate is established by a tree scan; firing before the change lands requires a planning-time tree observer (hence the activation fact is marked needs_new_observer).

values: a canonical documentation area directory exists in the tree (pre-existing or created by the planned change) without its index
a plan or diff touches the documentation tree, including any document at its root — discovery hint only, neither sufficient nor required for firing
documentation wording, or the local names of the canonical areas — discovery hint only, not an alternate trigger and not a gate

fires: A plan creates a canonical area with documents but no index.
A change deletes an area's index while the area still exists.
A canonical area already exists in the tree without its index, even if the current task does not touch it.
The documentation tree root itself has documents but no index.
doesNotFire: The area does not exist in the tree at all.
A generated output tree under the documentation tree has no index.
A non-canonical subdirectory inside an area (e.g. one holding two related documents) has no index.

neutralityNotes: The convention is about a documentation-tree discipline rather than code, so most of it neutralizes cleanly at role level (authored area, entry-point index, generated output). What could not be made neutral: (1) the concrete canonical areas and the index file name are pulled from the profile (two keys proposed, since the closed vocabulary has no documentation-tree keys); (2) the generated-output tree excluded by this check is NOT a profile value — roots.excluded is the one stack-wide union of never-scanned vendored/generated trees, while this rule's docs/dist/ exclusion is a rule-specific classification owned by the check itself (kept generically in core verification, concretely in bunOnly), so the core does not infer it from the global list; (3) the AsciiDoc document-identity header (title, :doc-id:, :status: attributes) and the sibling rule id planner.docs.adr-registry-derived remain bunOnly — the core keeps only 'full document identity like any authored document'; (4) the validator id docs_capability and the concrete discovery globs/task terms are bunOnly; (5) severity 3 uses the ATDD convention's own severity scale and is kept in core verification per the notProfileKeys rule. The 'rendered documentation navigates to' phrasing assumes the docs tree is published/rendered, which is a property of the documentation role, not of a stack.
